subject.title: feat: add lease-bound metadata to session spawns

question: Should OpenClaw core permanently expose and persist this Agentic OS-specific lease and session-orchestration RPC contract, or should the downstream orchestrator use an existing extension boundary with only a narrowly justified generic core seam?
rationale: The patch is not only a bug repair: it adds seven public Gateway methods, discovery metadata, persisted authority, and a new external workflow contract. Repository policy reserves this kind of core/protocol scope choice for explicit maintainer direction.

options.title: Narrow to a generic core seam
options.body: Recommended: define the smallest reusable authorization/session hook OpenClaw needs, then keep Agentic OS identifiers, lifecycle semantics, and orchestration-specific discovery in its owner repository.

options.title: Sponsor the core contract
options.body: Accept this as a supported core Gateway API, then require durable identity, versioned/documented compatibility behavior, and upgrade and reconnect proof before merge.

options.title: Keep it downstream
options.body: Close the core expansion and implement the workflow through the current plugin or downstream integration surface if no missing core API is demonstrated.

recommendation.title: Narrow to a generic core seam
recommendation.body: Recommended: define the smallest reusable authorization/session hook OpenClaw needs, then keep Agentic OS identifiers, lifecycle semantics, and orchestration-specific discovery in its owner repository.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision changes the public Gateway and core session-runtime boundary rather than only the submitted implementation.
